findings.title: V2 canManage() grants manage on all groups when admin only has the VIEW scope
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` falls through to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true if the caller is granted *either* `view` or `manage` on the type-level "Groups" resource. `canManage()` is what `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` enforces via `auth.groups().requireManage()`, and that endpoint both creates new top-level groups and (when an `id` is supplied) moves an existing sub-group to the top level. So an admin who was only granted a read-only all-groups `view` permission can create groups and restructure the group hierarchy. The per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly checks only `MANAGE`; the type-level method should do the same. Note the new Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` ("For V2 only: Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") was written to match this wrong behaviour and should be corrected as well. `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewGroups` grants all-groups VIEW but never asserts that group creation is still forbidden, so the escalation is not caught by the tests.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz Resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In the V2 implementation the per-group authorization `Resource` is created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` with the group's ID as the resource *name*; the resource's own `getId()` is an unrelated UUID generated by the resource store. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` nevertheless calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` (so `resourceStore.findByName(server, <resource uuid>)` never matches and it silently falls back to the type-level "Groups" resource) and then does `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. The returned set is consumed by `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` as `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` and by `getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`, both of which expect real group IDs to restrict the DB query to members of those groups. With resource UUIDs the membership subquery matches nothing, so e.g. an admin granted `view-members` on the all-groups resource gets an empty user list and a count of 0 even though `canView(user)` would succeed for every group member. The V1 implementation correctly derives the group ID from the resource name; V2 should use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission check and the returned set.

findings.title: findByType("Groups") cannot enumerate per-group resources because getOrCreateResource never sets a resource type
findings.body: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` enumerates group resources with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However the per-group resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (server-spi-private/.../AdminPermissionsSchema.java line 121) via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` followed only by `updateScopes(...)`; no `setType(...)` is ever called. The only resource with type "Groups" is the type-level "all groups" resource created in `init()` (which does `resource.setType(type)`). Consequently the callback is invoked at most once, for the "Groups" resource itself, and groups with individual `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are never discovered, so the group-based pre-filtering of user searches never works for them (results then depend solely on the post-filter over the page returned by the DB, which breaks pagination/completeness). Either set the type on resources created by `getOrCreateResource` or enumerate per-group resources another way.

findings.title: Any per-group permission shadows the all-groups permission for every other scope on that group
findings.body: `hasPermission(groupId, scopes...)` looks up the per-group resource by name and, if it exists, evaluates only the policies attached to that resource; the type-level "Groups" resource is consulted only when no per-group resource exists. The policy evaluator only collects policies directly attached to the given resource (the per-group resource has no type, so no type-based lookup happens). Therefore as soon as anyone creates a permission on a specific group for one scope (e.g. `view-members` for admin A), an admin B who holds `manage`/`view` on the all-groups resource loses those rights for that specific group, because the all-groups policies are no longer evaluated for it. The test `testManageAllGroups` only covers the case where no per-group resource exists ("fallback to all-groups permission"), so this is untested. The evaluation should consider both the per-group resource and the type-level resource (e.g. evaluate the all-groups permission when the per-group evaluation does not produce a decision for the requested scope), or document this as an explicit limitation.

findings.title: Group-based search restriction hides users granted via direct per-user permissions
findings.body: `searchForUser` now unconditionally sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` whenever `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. The JPA user provider turns this attribute into a hard `user IN (members of these groups)` restriction on the search query. In V2 an admin can simultaneously hold `view-members` on group G and a direct `view` permission on user Bob (Users resource type) who is not a member of G. With this change the DB query is restricted to members of G, so Bob is never returned by `GET /users` even though `UserPermissionsV2.canView(bob)` is true and `GET /users/{bob}` succeeds. The same applies to `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`. The group filter should only be applied when the admin has no other (per-user or type-level) user view grants, or the result sets need to be merged.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve names for Groups resources
findings.body: `getResourceName` only special-cases the `Users` resource type (returning "All users" or the username). For the newly added `Groups` type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, but per-group resources are created in `getOrCreateResource` without a display name and with the raw group ID as the name. Any representation that uses `getResourceName` (e.g. permission listings in the admin console) will therefore show `null`/empty names for group permissions, and the type-level "Groups" resource gets no "All groups" label analogous to "All users". A `Groups` branch resolving the group (and its path/name) should be added.

findings.title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers references the wrong method
findings.body: The new Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws `ForbiddenException` if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation (both V1 and V2) checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, which is a different scope (`manage-members` vs `manage-membership`). Similarly, the Javadoc of `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says "@return Stream of IDs" while the method returns a `Set<String>`. Since this interface is the contract other code relies on to pick the right check, the docs should name the correct methods/types.

findings.title: No negative assertions for scope separation (view vs manage, membership) in the new group tests
findings.body: The new test class only checks that granted scopes allow operations; it never asserts that a weaker scope does *not* grant a stronger one. In particular: after `createAllGroupsPermission(policy, Set.of(VIEW))` in `testViewGroups` there is no assertion that `groups().add(...)` is still 403 (which would have caught `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` granting on VIEW); `testManageGroupMembership` only verifies success after granting both the all-users `manage-group-membership` and the group `manage-membership` scope, never that joining is forbidden when only the user-side scope is present (so a `canManageMembership` that always returned true would pass); and there is no test that `view-members`/`manage-members` on all groups surfaces users in `GET /users` (which currently returns an empty list because resource UUIDs are used as group IDs). Please add these negative/combination cases.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the new Groups resource and scopes
findings.body: `init()` returns early when `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient()` already exists, and the new `Groups` type-level resource plus the `manage-membership`/`manage-members`/`view-members` scopes are only created in that initialisation path. Realms whose admin-permissions client was created before this change therefore have no "Groups" resource and no group scopes. For them `getResourceTypeResource(..., "Groups")` returns null and `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission` then calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` (NPE/500 on any group permission check), and creating a group permission fails in `getOrCreateResource` with `ModelException("No scopes found.")`. Even though the V2 feature is preview, some idempotent upgrade of the schema (create missing type resources/scopes when they are absent) is needed instead of the early return.

findings.title: switch on resourceType throws NPE for null resource type
findings.body: `getOrCreateResource` now does `switch (resourceType)` on a `String`. If `resourceType` is null (the previous code handled this by leaving `name` null and throwing the descriptive `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object with type [null] ...")`), a `switch` on a null String throws a bare `NullPointerException`, which surfaces as a 500 instead of a meaningful validation error. Guard for null before the switch (or include it in the `default` branch).

findings.title: manage-members cannot be used to create users under V2 because canCreateGroupMembers is gated on the V1 feature
findings.body: `createUser` falls back to `canCreateGroupMembers(rep)` when the caller lacks the users `manage` permission, which is the path that lets an admin holding `manage-members`/`manage-membership` on a group create a user directly into that group. That method starts with `if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) return false;` (the V1 flag). With only `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` enabled (the configuration this PR targets, since both versions of the feature cannot be enabled together), the new `manage-members`/`manage-membership` group scopes added here can never be used to create users, contradicting the scope semantics documented in `GroupPermissionEvaluator`. The check should also accept the V2 feature.
